_README: Spec 095 S3 — EDITOR-STATE OVERLAY. Hand-written, deliberately tiny, NEVER generated.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `dify-dsl-<version>.json` is generated from Dify's BACKEND pydantic models
(schemas/gen_schema.py), so it can only ever describe fields the backend models. Dify's editor
keeps additional state on some node bodies that the backend never sees — and a workflow missing
that state imports cleanly, passes every linter, and then CANNOT BE PUBLISHED, because the editor's
own pre-publish checklist rejects it. That class is invisible to a backend-derived schema by
construction, which is why it needs a separate, human-maintained file instead of a patch to the
generated one (a patch would be erased on the next regeneration anyway).
WARN-FIRST, BY CONSTRUCTION. lint_node_bodies.py feeds these findings into its `warnings` channel,
which is printed to stderr and NEVER folded into the exit code. That is not a policy anyone has to
remember: the linter is one of the four `LINTERS` the builder gates ③ on (lintClean requires all
four == 0) and it also runs in pre-commit, so a rule that moved the exit code would instantly
become a hard gate on a rule derived from another project's frontend internals. Promote a rule to
hard-failing only after it has run warn-only across real builds — the same 3-phase discipline
lint_node_bodies.py itself shipped under (spec 038: unwired → measure → wire).
RULE KINDS. `kind` selects the check; omitting it means "must_cover" (the original shape), so
older rules keep working untouched. A kind this linter does not know is SKIPPED, never fatal —
a newer overlay must degrade to silence on an older checkout.
- must_cover         a field that must expose every name declared elsewhere in the body
- json_string_values a typed value list whose object/array rows must hold a JSON *string*
- inert_keys         a sub-block written with keys the backend model does not carry at all
`node_type` accepts "*" for a rule that is not tied to one node type.
SCOPE NOTE. This pass runs BEFORE the generated-schema gate in lint_node_bodies.py, so it still
speaks for node types whose def is missing or an `_error` dump-stub (`http-request` today). It
used to run after, which made it dead code for exactly the types it was written to cover.
THE BAR FOR ADDING A RULE (keep this file small):
1. the field is absent from the generated $defs for that node type — otherwise the schema gates it;
2. its absence is USER-VISIBLE and blocking (publish refused / step broken), not cosmetic;
3. `evidence` cites the exact vendor source that proves it, AND a real observation on a real
instance with the version — a source read alone has been wrong before.
MAINTENANCE. Every rule is pinned to a Dify version. When vendor/dify-src is bumped, re-read each
`evidence` path: if the mechanism changed, fix or delete the rule. A stale rule here is worse than
no rule — it teaches a shape Dify no longer wants.

editor_state_rules.why: The editor builds this node's OUTPUT variable list from `data.variables` ONLY — never from `body`. Without it the node exposes zero outputs, every downstream reference reads as "invalid variable", and Dify blocks publishing.
editor_state_rules.fix: Add one entry per body/params/headers item plus the built-in raw object: {variable: <name>, label: body|param|header, value_type: <same as the item>, value_selector: [], required: <same>} and {variable: _webhook_raw, label: raw, value_type: object, value_selector: [], required: true}. Working example: templates/patterns/webhook-per-row-notify.yml
evidence: vendor/dify-src @ 1.13.0-42 — web/app/components/workflow/hooks/use-checklist.ts flags a used-but-absent variable as errorMsg.invalidVariable
OBSERVED on Dify 1.15 (2026-08-12, spec 095 S0): importing the same workflow with `variables` added makes the checklist's 「Biến không hợp lệ」 item disappear; without it, publish is refused

editor_state_rules.why: The backend accepts BOTH a real mapping and its JSON-string form (DefaultValue.validate_value_type json.loads a str), so import, every linter and a green Test Run all agree the file is fine. The EDITOR does not: it passes the value straight to Monaco, which requires a string — createTextBuffer() falls through to `factory.create(...)` on a non-string and throws `TypeError: $.create is not a function`. The node's config panel then goes blank the moment anyone CLICKS the node, and the workflow can no longer be edited.
editor_state_rules.fix: Quote it: `value: '{}'` not `value: {}`, `value: '[]'` not `value: []`, `value: '{"a":1}'` not a nested mapping. That is the form Dify's own editor writes (getDefaultValueByType returns the STRING '{}'), and the backend json.loads it back — so the quoted form is correct on both sides. Worked example: .claude/skills/dify-build/references/error-strategy.yml node '1754000000007'
evidence: vendor/dify-src @ 1.15 — web/app/components/workflow/nodes/_base/components/error-handle/error-handle-on-panel.tsx: the panel renders <DefaultValue forms={default_value}> straight from the DSL, never through getDefaultValue()

vendor/dify-src @ 1.15 — .../error-handle/default-value.tsx: type object/array[*] renders <CodeEditor language={json} value={form.value}> with no isJSONStringifyBeauty, so the raw value reaches Monaco
vendor/dify-src @ 1.15 — web/node_modules/monaco-editor/esm/vs/editor/common/model/textModel.js createTextBuffer(): `else { factory = value }` then `factory.create(defaultEOL)` — the exact throw
vendor/dify-src @ 1.15 — .../error-handle/utils.ts getDefaultValueByType(): VarType.object returns the STRING '{}' — the editor's own writer proves the intended encoding
vendor/dify-src @ 1.15 — api/core/workflow/nodes/base/entities.py DefaultValue.validate_value_type: `converter: self._parse_json` accepts the string form, so quoting is safe for the backend too

OBSERVED on Dify 1.15 (2026-08-13): projects/_drafts/build_requirement_news_automation_2 — 9 http-request nodes each carrying `- {key: headers, type: object, value: {}}` imported clean, passed all 4 linters and ran green; clicking ANY of them blanked the panel. Quoting to '{}' fixed all 9.

editor_state_rules.why: `max_*_timeout` are NOT the timeout. They are the UI slider's upper CAP, seeded at 0 on every fresh node by Dify's default.ts — which is why they show up in exported DSL and read like the real field names. The backend model HttpRequestNodeTimeout carries only connect/read/write and drops the max_* keys silently, so a node written this way has NO timeout configured: it falls back to connect=10 / read=600 / write=600. A hung receiver then stalls the run for TEN MINUTES instead of the seconds the author wrote, and nothing anywhere reports it.
editor_state_rules.fix: Write the binding keys: `timeout: { connect: 10, read: 30, write: 10 }` (add `ssl_verify: true` alongside). Keep max_* only if you also set the real values and genuinely want to lower the editor's slider ceiling.
evidence: vendor/dify-src @ 1.15 — api/core/workflow/nodes/http_request/entities.py: `class HttpRequestNodeTimeout` declares connect/read/write ONLY; max_* appear nowhere on the node model
vendor/dify-src @ 1.15 — api/core/workflow/nodes/http_request/node.py get_default_config(): max_* exist only in the /default-workflow-block-configs payload the FRONTEND store reads for slider caps

vendor/dify-src @ 1.15 — web/app/components/workflow/nodes/http/components/timeout/index.tsx: `value={connect}` vs `max={max_connect_timeout || …}` — the two roles, side by side; onChange writes `connect`
vendor/dify-src @ 1.15 — api/configs/feature/__init__.py: the fallbacks a dropped timeout lands on — HTTP_REQUEST_MAX_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=10, MAX_READ_TIMEOUT=600, MAX_WRITE_TIMEOUT=600
